_note: TEMPLATE. Copy to profile.json and fill it in: `cp data/profile.example.json data/profile.json`, then run `python -m core.profile checkfill` to list everything still unset. Anything left as FILL_ME is treated as MISSING — the extension will not autofill it and will surface the question instead of guessing, which is the intended failure mode. Booleans render as Yes/No via core/profile.py.

address._country_full_note: Workday's country dropdown has 251 options and matches on exact text, where the US reads 'United States of America'. It also pre-selects a country from your IP, so this is set explicitly on every fill rather than left at its default.

identity._location_display_note: How a single-box location field should read. Many ATS location pickers search server-side on what is typed, so use the form their dropdown expects, e.g. 'City, State, Country'.
identity._based_in_us_note: Answers the Yes/No form of the residence question ('Do you live in the US, or plan to by your start date?', 'Are you based in a US-equivalent timezone?'). Separate from address.country because those controls take Yes/No, not a country name.

_work_authorization_note: REVIEW EVERY VALUE HERE BEFORE YOUR FIRST RUN. These answers are submitted to real employers and a wrong default is worse than no answer. The booleans below are only placeholders to show the shape, not a recommendation.

employment._note: Kept for the single-value taxonomy rules ('current employer', 'current title'). The full list lives in work_history below; these should mirror work_history[0].

_work_history_note: Required by Workday, which will not advance past its 'My Experience' step without a full work history. Greenhouse/Lever/Ashby never ask for this, which is why it did not exist before.
_by_stream_note: OPTIONAL per-resume-track wording. Each resume (quant/ds/tech/ai) describes the same jobs in a different vocabulary, so the form must match the PDF attached to it or the pair reads as embellishment. Put ONLY the keys that differ inside by_stream.<tag>; anything absent falls through to the default written alongside it. Resolved once per application by core.profile.resolve_stream(), keyed on the tag pick_resume() already chose. Employer, title, dates and location are FACTS — never vary them by stream.

work_history.title: FILL_ME
work_history._date_note: YYYY-MM. Workday's date control is a split month/year spinner, so the pipeline needs the parts, not a display string like 'January 2024'.
work_history._end_note: null means current. Tick `current` instead of inventing an end date — Workday removes its End Date field entirely when 'I currently work here' is checked.

education._school_note: Use the school's full formal name and avoid parentheticals/acronyms. ATS school pickers run a server-side search on exactly this string, and a bracketed acronym returns zero matches — see the type-to-search notes in extension/fill.js.
education._major_alternates_note: OPTIONAL fallbacks, tried in order when `major` is not offered. ATS field-of-study pickers are fixed vocabularies, not free text, and a perfectly ordinary major may simply be absent — Adobe's Workday list has 320 entries and no 'Computer Science'. Which substitute is TRUE is a claim about your degree, so it is read from here and never guessed. Leave empty and the field is surfaced for you, with the closest options the walker saw named in the report.
education._gpa_note: If you studied on a non-4.0 scale, note that US forms ask for a 4.0 one — often as a fixed pick-list ('4.0 out of 4.0' … '3.4 out of 4.0') that a 10-point or percentage mark matches nothing in. Which 4.0-scale number is TRUE of your transcript is a claim about your degree, so it is read from here and never converted for you: put your own equivalent in `gpa` and add the other wordings under answer_alternates['education.gpa'].
education._gpa_graduate_note: OPTIONAL. Answers the 'GPA (Graduate)' / 'GPA (Doctorate)' rows some forms ask unconditionally alongside the undergraduate one — SpaceX asks all three and marks each required. `gpa` above is the UNDERGRADUATE figure and must not be filled into these: that would claim a degree you do not hold. Set it to the not-applicable wording, or leave it out and those rows are surfaced for you.
education._standardized_tests_note: OPTIONAL. SAT / ACT / GRE score pick-lists, which some US employers make required fields for new grads. Every such list carries a not-applicable row, but whether you sat the test is a fact about you, so it is read from here and never guessed. Leave it out and the fields are surfaced for you.
education._start_date_note: OPTIONAL. Workday's education block has a 'From' year alongside the graduation year, and nothing else in this profile can supply it — a course length is not a fact about you, so it is never inferred. Leave it out and that box stays empty for you to fill; set it (YYYY or YYYY-MM) and it is filled like any other field.

_skills_note: OPTIONAL. Workday's 'Type to Add Skills' is a fixed vocabulary, not free text, so these are matched against its list and the ones it does not offer are reported rather than forced. SPELL EACH ONE THE WAY THE ATS DOES: a result counts only if it IS the entry or the entry with a parenthetical (so 'Python' finds 'Python (Programming Language)'), because a looser rule would tick 'Python IDLE' or 'Maya Python' — a different claim than the one on the resume. Where the vocabulary words it differently, put THEIR wording here: 'ETL' is stocked as 'Data ETL', and 'C++' as 'C++ Programming Language' (searching 'C++' also fails outright, since the server strips the '++'). The per-skill miss reasons in the fill report tell you which is which. Put ONLY skills that are on the resume being attached — the form and the PDF are read side by side, and a skill on one but not the other reads as padding. Never add a skill because a posting asked for it. Per-track lists work exactly like work_history's by_stream: anything absent falls through to `list`. Only the first `maxSkills` (8) are entered, since each one costs a full walk of the vocabulary.

preferences._target_roles_note: Free text, used to ground Claude-drafted essay answers (bridge/drafter.py). Say what you are aiming FOR, e.g. 'backend and platform engineering roles in the US'.
preferences.work_arrangement: Open to remote, hybrid, or onsite

attestations._note: Yes/No attestation-style questions. Booleans render Yes/No. Defaults below are the common case, but they are ASSERTIONS ABOUT YOU — read every one.
attestations._sms_consent_note: Whether to opt in when a board asks to text you about the application. Distinct from data_privacy_consent, which is the terms/privacy agreement.

eeo._note: US voluntary self-identification. Left as FILL_ME on purpose: there is no sane default for someone else's demographics, and every field here is optional on the form. Fill in what you want auto-answered and leave the rest — anything unset is simply surfaced for you to answer by hand. Declining is always a valid answer; most forms offer a 'I don't wish to answer' option you can paste in verbatim.

affiliations._note: Prior/related-connection disclosure questions. All No assumes you are not applying to a current or former employer, or to a company where you have a relative. If you ever do, add a per-company override in taxonomy.yaml so it gets surfaced instead of auto-answered.

_local_resume_source._note: Resumes are copied from this LOCAL folder into the gitignored resumes/ cache that the extension reads for its DataTransfer attach. Point base_dir at wherever your PDFs live, then run `python -m core.resumes sync-local`. Each track's local_source is relative to base_dir.

_resume_tracks_note: One resume per specialisation; the scraper picks a track per role by keyword overlap against the job title and description (title weighted 2x). Keep 1 track if you only have one resume — set its keywords to [] and make it default_resume_tag. The keyword lists below are generic and safe to keep as-is. drive_id is optional and only used by the Google Drive sync path.

answer_alternates._note: OPTIONAL fallback answers, keyed by the taxonomy value_key they stand in for. The fill engine offers your own value above first; only if the control's options match none of it does it walk this list, in order, keeping the first the control accepts. Two uses: (a) other wordings of the SAME answer, for ATS vocabularies that phrase it differently, and (b) a ranked list of answers you find equally true, most-preferred first. Delete the examples and write your own — an answer you would not actually give does not belong here.
eeo.veteran_status: I am not a protected veteran
work_authorization.authorized_us: I am authorized to work in the United States for any employer
